title: PTS, XYZ and ReCap
sub: Plain text, Autodesk projects and scan-to-BIM
cards/0/title: As simple as it gets: XYZ and PTS
cards/0/body:
XYZ is text: each line holds x y z, sometimes r g b too.
PTS (a Leica format): the first line is the point count, then x y z, intensity and r g b.

Anything can open it, but it is huge and slow: every digit is a separate byte.
cards/1/q: Which PTS line is the point count?
cards/1/explain: The first line says how many points follow. The fourth number on each line is intensity, then the color.
cards/2/q: Why are PTS and XYZ so big?
cards/2/options/0: Every digit is written as a text character: a point takes dozens of bytes instead of 20–36
cards/2/explain: “12.402” is 6 bytes as text, while in LAS the same coordinate is a 4-byte integer.
cards/3/title: RCP and RCS: point clouds in Autodesk
cards/3/body:
ReCap is Autodesk’s point cloud software. RCS is a single scan converted into a fast indexed format. RCP is a project that references a set of RCS files.

RCP is what you load into Revit, Navisworks and AutoCAD.
cards/4/q: A colleague sent only an .rcp, and the cloud will not open. Why?
cards/4/options/0: RCP is a project of references; the points themselves live in .rcs files that were not included
cards/4/explain: Same story as an OBJ without textures: a file of references without the things it references.
cards/5/body:
Scans from different stations are stitched into one cloud: that is registration. Then the cloud is cleaned and classified, and walls and pipes are modeled from it: that is scan-to-BIM.

This is how teams check whether everything was built as designed, or model an old building before renovation.
cards/6/q: Put the scan-to-BIM steps in order
cards/6/items/1: Registration: stitch scans into one cloud
cards/6/items/3: Modeling BIM objects from the cloud
cards/6/explain: From points to smart objects, and back to checking.
